title: CENTCOM Destroys Five Iranian Oil Tankers After IRGC's Second Attempted Strike on US Warship in Two Days
detail: CENTCOM said US forces destroyed five Iranian crude oil carriers — M/T Kaviz, M/T Charminar, M/T Horizon 1, and M/T Riesco in the Gulf of Oman, and M/T Derya near Kharg Island — after the IRGC attempted to strike a US Navy warship with ballistic missiles for the second time in two days; the warship evaded both attempts and no American personnel were harmed. US forces directed the tankers' crews to abandon ship before rendering the vessels inoperable; no casualties were reported. CENTCOM described the ships as part of a 'multibillion-dollar shadow network' financing the IRGC. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said: 'Iran continues to try to hit US naval ships, and for every time they do that or try to do that, they're going to lose tankers.' Separately, a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile roughly 52km southeast of Al-Faw, Iraq (crew reported safe), and a vessel was reported listing off Port Rashid, Dubai, possibly from water ingress after an attack.

media.caption: One of five Iranian crude oil carriers destroyed by US forces, Sept 8, 2026

confidenceReason: CENTCOM confirmed the tanker strikes and vessel names on the record; corroborated across Western and Middle Eastern outlets with consistent details.

title: IRGC Fires 20 Ballistic Missiles at Jordan's Al-Azraq Air Base; Claims Strikes on Two US Destroyers CENTCOM Calls 'Completely False'
detail: In retaliation for the tanker strikes, the IRGC fired 20 ballistic missiles at Jordan's Al-Azraq (Muwaffaq Salti) Air Base, which hosts US military assets. Jordan's armed forces said they intercepted and destroyed 18 of the missiles, with 2 falling in unpopulated areas and no casualties. The IRGC claimed the missiles 'struck the maintenance, preparation, and deployment sites of F-35, F-16, and F-15 fighter jets, as well as their shelters,' inflicting heavy damage — a claim incompatible with Jordan's account of two impacts in empty ground. Iranian state-aligned media separately claimed the IRGC struck two US Navy destroyers, DDG-119 and DDG-53, causing 'significant damage,' plus 8 commercial tankers in the region. CENTCOM called the destroyer claim 'completely FALSE,' saying 'all IRGC attempted attacks failed.' A Trump administration official said Jordan's integrated air and missile defenses prevented casualties.

media.caption: Al-Azraq (Muwaffaq Salti) Air Base, Jordan, target of the Sept 8 IRGC missile barrage

confidenceReason: The missile count and interception figures come from Jordan's official account and are corroborated across outlets; the IRGC's claims of destroyer damage and hangar destruction are single-source Iranian state media claims explicitly denied by CENTCOM.

title: IRGC Claims Capture of US Navy Unmanned Underwater Vehicle Near Strait of Hormuz; Pentagon Says It Had Already Malfunctioned
detail: Iran's IRGC announced Tuesday evening it had captured a US military unmanned underwater vehicle at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz in what it called a 'complex intelligence and operational' action, identifying the craft as an Anduril Dive-LD — a roughly 6-meter, ~$2.5M autonomous submersible capable of mine countermeasures, seabed mapping, and infrastructure inspection, with up to 10 days' endurance and a 6,000m depth rating. A Pentagon spokesperson disputed Iran's narrative, saying the vehicle 'had malfunctioned a day ago' and was 'an older model that neither collected sensitive data nor carried any classified sonar or radar equipment.' Anduril confirmed the loss of one vessel but downplayed its significance, noting the Dive-LD 'is an attritable autonomous system, meaning it is designed from the outset to operate in dangerous environments where loss of the vehicle is an expected possibility.'

media.caption: The Anduril Dive-LD unmanned underwater vehicle Iran claims to have captured near the Strait of Hormuz

confidenceReason: Anduril confirmed the loss of one vehicle, corroborating that something was lost, but the Pentagon disputes Iran's 'capture' framing and says the device had already malfunctioned — a direct contradiction between IRGC and US accounts.
